ai.title: Add desktop download click analytics event
ai.summary: Added `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_CLICKED` to `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`. This event tracks clicks on desktop download CTAs across the home hero, products row, and `/desktop` page. The payload includes `location` for the CTA, `platform` for the build, and a `repeat` flag to identify swallowed double-clicks.

eli5.text: When you click a download button for the desktop app, whether you're on the homepage, browsing products, or visiting the dedicated desktop page, the site now records that click and which spot it came from, along with your operating system. If you double-click quickly because you're unsure the download started, the site counts the extra click as a retry rather than a fresh attempt, giving the team a clearer read on how well the download buttons are working. The change is in place and live today.

ai.title: Fix nested gitignore pattern matching
ai.summary: Replaced manual gitignore pattern rebasing with a directory-aware ignore chain in `project-file-tree.ts`. The `parseGitignore` function now returns raw patterns, and a new `isIgnored` helper evaluates files against parent directory scopes using `DirIgnore` structures. This fixes incorrect matching for nested `.gitignore` files that previously failed due to flawed path rewriting logic.

eli5.text: The assistant's file browser was incorrectly hiding files and folders when there were multiple ignore rules stacked in different directories. If you opened a project and some files that should have been visible were missing, that was the bug. The fix rewrites how nested ignore rules are combined so that each directory's rules are applied independently, and the results are layered together instead of mashed into one path-rewrite. The change is live today, so a project with nested.gitignore or.codebuffignore files now shows the correct contents.

facts: Added 2026-08-03 on behavioural rather than statistical evidence, these are below the >=20-account bar the block above uses, so they qualify on what their accounts DO instead.

The .qd.je pair: 14 accounts each, every one registered on a SINGLE day (impact 2026-07-10, fincy 2026-07-13), and 13 of the 28 surfaced in the silent-endpoint scan. A same-day mint of 14 accounts is not a mailbox provider signing up users.

ai.title: Block proxyvpn.cn and qd.je domains on behavioural evidence
ai.summary: Added proxyvpn.cn, impact.qd.je, and fincy.qd.je to DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS in common/src/util/disposable-email.ts. Domains qualify via silent-endpoint abuse and same-day account bursts despite falling below the >=20-account statistical threshold. Deliberately excluded dns-proxy.com and proximus.lu to prevent false positives from real ISPs. Blocklist relies on domain-specific entries rather than substring matching to avoid collateral damage.

eli5.text: Accounts created at proxyvpn.cn, impact.qd.je, and fincy.qd.je can no longer be used, because these domains were behaving like temporary throwaway mailboxes even though only a handful of accounts appeared on them. Youd notice this when someone signing up with one of those email addresses is immediately rejected, since the system blocks new accounts from these three domains outright. The system now requires a real, active email provider instead of a proxy or single-day signup service.

ai.title: Add x-freebuff-takeover-instance-id header constant
ai.summary: Added `FREEBUFF_TAKEOVER_INSTANCE_HEADER` (`x-freebuff-takeover-instance-id`) to `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`. Provides an explicit escape hatch for Desktop's 'Use it here' action when the single-slot holder is alive on an unreachable machine or window. The server only honors this header if the instance ID matches the holder identified in the rejection, preventing stale cards from terminating unrelated tabs.

eli5.text: If you're using the desktop app and try to take over a single-slot session that's still technically alive on another machine or window you can't close, there's now a new header-based escape hatch that tells the server to end that specific tab and hand the slot to you. The server only honors this takeover when the instance ID you provide matches the exact holder the system just rejected you from, so clicking a stale card can't accidentally disconnect a tab you never saw. This is in place and live today, providing a targeted override for Desktop's 'Use it here' action without risking unrelated tabs.

ai.title: Add FREEBUFFSESSIONGRACEMS for session drain window
ai.summary: Added FREEBUFF_SESSION_GRACE_MS constant (30 minutes) to define the drain window after a session's expires_at. This allows the gate to serve in-flight agent runs while blocking new prompts, distinguishing finishing runs from dead tabs. The client uses this to stop heartbeats once the row passes the grace period, syncing with server-side getSessionGraceMs(). Scope limited to common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts.

eli5.text: After a session expires, there's now a 30-minute buffer period where active tasks can finish but new ones won't start. This prevents your work from being cut off if you're still using the app when your session ends, while stopping new work from starting once that window closes. You'd notice this if your session expired but you could still finish typing a response before the app fully logged you out. This change is live today.

ai.title: Freebuff streak line switches to terminal-safe glyphs and layout fit
ai.summary: The Freebuff landing streak line now passes terminal-safe bullet and middle-dot glyphs (`•`/`·`) and measures the streak against the real heading string to decide whether it shares the heading row, replacing the old fixed 50-column width check with `fitsFreebuffStreakOnHeadingRow`. `LandingHeadingRow` is added in `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx` (exported for layout tests) and `StreakInlineLine` drops its `marginTop` prop, drawing identical spans in both placements. The shared `getFreebuffStreakLine` in `common/src/util/freebuff-streak-line.ts` now takes an optional `FreebuffStreakDotChars` argument so the CLI can supply glyphs that survive font fallbacks while Desktop keeps `●`/`○`.

changes.what: Added exported `LandingHeadingRow` combining the heading title and optional streak via `streakSpans`; replaced the space-between flex row prone to flush rendering and renderer overflow with a single text using an explicit inline gap.
